description: The four places an XML document can hide a value, each escaping differently: element text and attributes replace ampersands and angle brackets with entities, a comment escapes nothing, and CDATA escapes nothing at all. Namespaced elements carry their prefix in the tag, so a pipeline keying on plain element names sees a different string. A reader that walks only text nodes leaks everything else.

slots.name: attrEmail
slots.label: email_address
slots.note: Carried in an attribute rather than element text. A reader that walks only text nodes never sees it.

slots.name: commentEmail
slots.label: email_address
slots.note: Inside an XML comment. Comments are invisible to a renderer but present in the bytes, so a leak here survives every visual review.

slots.name: cdataCard
slots.label: payment_card
slots.note: Inside CDATA, where nothing is escaped. The one place in an XML document where a value's decoded and source offsets coincide.

slots.name: entityName
slots.label: organization_name
slots.note: Contains an ampersand and angle brackets, so it is written as entities and occupies far more bytes in the file than in its decoded form.

slots.name: serial
slots.label: bank_account
slots.note: A hardware serial under an element named 'serial'. Nothing vouches for it, so detecting it is over-redaction.

slots.name: nsEmail
slots.label: email_address
slots.note: Inside a namespace-prefixed element, <c:email>. A pipeline matching on the element name 'email' for context sees 'c:email' instead and loses the boost.
